# Entities

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_reference.py from the code. Do not edit by hand: change the code or strings.json and run the script. -->

Every entity Roomba+ can create, with the id it gets. `<robot>` stands for your robot's name as Home Assistant writes it in an id: a robot called *Kitchen Roomba* gives `sensor.kitchen_roomba_battery`. The ids are English in every language, so an automation works whatever language Home Assistant is set to.

**Robots** says which robots can get the entity: Classic (local connection), Prime (iRobot cloud) or both. Whether yours gets it also depends on the model and on the options: a robot without a mop has no mop sensors, and some entities exist only while their option is on ([Options](options.md)). **Starts** says *Off* for entities that are created disabled: turn them on on the device page. **Category** is where the device page lists them.

An entity whose id ends in `<…>` exists once per room, area, part, favourite or schedule.

[Sensors](#sensors) · [Binary sensors](#binary-sensors) · [Buttons](#buttons) · [Selects](#selects) · [Switches](#switches) · [Images (maps)](#images-maps) · [Calendars](#calendars) · [To-do lists](#to-do-lists) · [Events](#events) · [Device tracker](#device-tracker) · [Vacuum](#vacuum)
